task.prompt: Describe the standard protocol for emergency patient triage in a hospital setting.

candidates.output_text: Emergency triage involves a rapid assessment of patient severity to determine treatment priority. Medical staff evaluate vital signs, chief complaints, and visible injuries to assign a triage category. Protocols like the Emergency Severity Index use a five-level system ranging from immediate resuscitation to non-urgent care.

Patient triage in emergency departments follows a structured protocol for severity assessment and priority assignment. Each patient undergoes a rapid diagnosis screening that evaluates their condition against established triage criteria. The emergency team uses standardized assessment tools to classify patients into priority levels, ensuring that the most critical cases receive immediate attention while lower-severity patients are queued appropriately.
Hospitals use triage to sort patients. Emergency cases get seen first based on how severe their condition is. Doctors do an assessment and decide priority.
